title: Networking: sockets, `HttpClient` and HTTP calls in the standard library

videos.script: Every program in this course so far has talked to itself. This lesson connects two of them, both on your own machine, so nothing leaves it. {{socket}} At the bottom is a socket: a pipe of bytes between two programs. One listens, one connects, and each wraps the bytes in the readers and writers of lesson 19. {{server}} On top of that sits HTTP, and the JDK has a small server for it. A few lines answer requests for books, one virtual thread per request. {{client}} Then the other side, HttpClient. Ask once and wait, or ask four times at once and join the answers, with the futures of lesson 16. {{fail}} And what goes wrong: nobody listening, an answer that never comes, and the not found that is an answer, not an error.
